expectations.text: Flags the three new columns added to the reviews table and says this per-review data belongs in its own table keyed by review_id
expectations.evidence: FRAMING: cross-module write → container.reviewRepo. Finding 5 is titled «Модуль пише в чужу таблицю — межа модуля порушена, хоч depcruise мовчить» and is about `repository.ts:24-68` touching `t.reviews`, not about the ALTER TABLE lines. It offers «два законні варіанти, обидва краще за поточний»: (1) `review_annotations` side table, (2) «Якщо колонки лишаються на `reviews` — ходити через `container.reviewRepo`». Option 2 explicitly blesses the three new columns staying on `reviews`, so the review never objects to the columns as such — it objects to who writes them. The ALTER TABLE lines (`0043_review_annotations.sql:7-9`) are never flagged.

expectations.text: Gives the operational reason for keeping reviews narrow — it is the hottest table and an ALTER rewrites/locks it, killing a run in flight — rather than a generic appeal to normalisation or tidiness
expectations.evidence: No operational reason anywhere: no mention of `reviews` being hot, of table rewrite, of ACCESS EXCLUSIVE / lock duration, or of a run dying mid-flight. The side-table option is justified only by ownership («модуль володіє своїми таблицями») and by «зникає `UPDATE` по чужому рядку». The non-CONCURRENTLY `CREATE INDEX ... ON reviews` is discussed (finding 11) purely as schema-drift and hand-written-SQL evidence, never as a locking risk.

expectations.text: Flags the new ON DELETE CASCADE foreign keys and says new ones should be RESTRICT, with the owning service deleting children explicitly
expectations.evidence: Only the single spectacular FK is flagged. Finding 3 covers `schema.excerpt.ts:28-30` (`annotation_author_id → users`) and recommends `onDelete: 'set null'`. The two other new cascades (`0043_review_annotations.sql:13-14`, workspace_id and review_id on annotation_attachments) are never questioned — they are cited approvingly in finding 6 as the FK that «перевіряє лише існування `reviews.id`». No general rule for new FKs, no RESTRICT, no owning-service-deletes-children.

expectations.text: Does NOT endorse the cascades or recommend matching the surrounding schema's cascading style — the existing cascades are grandfathered, and consistency is the wrong instinct here
expectations.evidence: Finding 3 argues from the surrounding schema's cascading style: «Каскади в цій схемі свідомо йдуть тільки по власнику (`workspace_id`, `pr_id` — server/src/db/schema/reviews.ts:11-18), і жодна таблиця не каскадить по «автору»». That treats the ambient owner-cascade pattern as deliberate and correct, which is exactly the endorsement the assertion excludes — and it validates the two new owner-shaped cascades on `annotation_attachments` by implication.

notes: Technically strong and accurate — every repo claim verified (0000_init.sql really has zero IF NOT EXISTS, OkResponse really is unused, knowledge.ts:77 composite tenant index, reviews/repository.ts:5-8 ownership comment) — but it misses both team decisions. The columns are framed as a module-boundary problem whose fix may legitimately leave them on `reviews`, and the cascades are reduced to the one author_id FK, defended by appeal to the surrounding owner-cascade style. Judgment call recorded explicitly: a8-no-cascade-endorsement is failed on that appeal, not on any sentence recommending a cascade be added.
